report.summary: Chunk 4 of render.py: defines helper functions for HTML rendering of reachability, switches, and gate data.

handoff.purpose: Define helper functions for HTML rendering: absent section, counts bar, legends, entry table, module table, test-only table, broken entry table, switch tables, and reconciliation block.

symbols.name: _counts_bar
symbols.note: Generates HTML div with counts for various categories.

symbols.name: _class_legend
symbols.note: Generates HTML legend for module classes from CLASSES.

symbols.name: _entry_table
symbols.note: Generates HTML table of entry points grouped by kind.

symbols.name: _module_table
symbols.note: Generates HTML table of modules grouped by classification, with open/closed details.

symbols.name: _test_only_table
symbols.note: Generates HTML details element for modules reached only by tests.

symbols.name: _broken_entry_table
symbols.note: Generates HTML details element for broken entry points.

symbols.name: _switch_tables
symbols.note: Generates multiple HTML sections for dark switches, conflicting defaults, dark params, drift, and dynamic reads.

symbols.name: _reconciliation
symbols.note: Computes reconciliation between gate and table counts.

claims.text: This half of the map is hand-written on purpose: no scanner derives it, so nothing was generated in its place. It is missing, not empty.
claims.why: The claim about the map being hand-written and not scanner-derived refers to a context outside this chunk; no scanner logic is present to verify.

claims.text: The headline the page owes the reader: not 'islands', which is one of three unreached classes, but every module no entry point gets to. island + orphan + unknown + shim, and the tiles beside it add up to exactly this.
claims.why: The code computes 'gate_unreached' count and displays it; the comment describes the grouping of unreached classes, which matches the code's logic.

claims.text: The alarms open by default; 'reachable' and 'test' are the long tail and stay folded, because a page that dumps 88 test files first is a page whose reader never scrolls to the seven islands.
claims.why: The code sets open_attr based on cls being in ('island','orphan','unknown','shim'), and order puts 'reachable' and 'test' last without open attribute.

claims.text: Modules whose only importer is a test, as their own class. This is the population that used to be silently green. The rule that a test counts as intent is kept -- these do not fail the gate -- but the consequence of the rule is now a list with a number on it, because 'wired to nothing but a test' is precisely the state that grew to 55 unnoticed the last time it was invisible.
claims.why: The claim about historical behavior and the gate not failing is not verifiable from this chunk; only the rendering logic is present.

claims.text: Nothing reaches these from any entry point; a test imports them. The gate reports them under 'TEST ONLY' and does NOT block on them — landing a test is evidence somebody means to wire the thing, and a gate that fails over that gets turned off. It is a count that has to keep moving toward zero, not an alarm.
claims.why: The claim about gate behavior (not blocking, counting toward zero) refers to logic outside this chunk; not verifiable here.

claims.text: A [project.scripts] target naming a module or a function that does not exist. It raises on invocation, so it is not a way in and nothing behind it is reached through it.
claims.why: The claim about the source of broken entries and their runtime behavior is not verifiable from this chunk; only rendering is present.

claims.text: Default off, and no read site falls back to a usable value: the code path does not run in normal operation.
claims.where: comment inside _switch_tables for dark env switches
claims.why: The claim about defaults and fallback values is not verifiable from this chunk; only rendering logic is present.

claims.text: The same variable resolves to different values in different modules. A status screen can report a setting the harness does not run.
claims.why: The claim about conflicting defaults and status screen behavior is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Gate vocabulary only. Safety postures (dry_run, force, overwrite) are deliberately not counted: force=False is a default, not a hidden feature.
claims.why: The claim about safety postures being excluded is not verifiable from this chunk; only rendering logic is present.

claims.text: The gate's numbers against the table's, computed rather than asserted. This block used to be prose explaining why the two halves of the page disagreed — and the explanation predicted the gate's island count would be SMALLER than the table's when it was in fact nearly twice as large, because the two halves ran different scanners. There is one scanner now, so every number below is a subtraction over the same walk and any inconsistency here is arithmetic, not interpretation.
claims.why: The claim about historical disagreement and current single scanner is not verifiable from this chunk; only variable assignments are present.

observations.what: The function _counts_bar uses a list of tuples with status, value, label, but the first two entries are hardcoded divs for 'modules' and 'gate_unreached' before iterating over cells.
In _entry_table, the variable 'by_kind' is typed as dict[str, list[dict]] but the type hint is not used in the code; it's a comment.
In _module_table, the order list includes 'entry' and 'reachable' but the comment says 'reachable' and 'test' are folded; 'entry' is not mentioned in the comment.
The function _reconciliation only assigns variables from data and does not yet produce any output; the function appears incomplete.

The comment in _counts_bar about 'gate_unreached' being the sum of island+orphan+unknown+shim is accurate based on the code: the tile is separate from the cells list which includes those four categories.
